text:
amy.k: FYI customer FinServX (private) reporting high tail latency today. They say egress from their onprem NAT is routing to eu-1 proxy intermittently, even though most traffic should hit apac-1. Symptoms started after a network maintenance at ~03:20 UTC.
vikram: do we have a trace_id or example request ts so we can correlate?
amy.k: trace_id=tr-2026-03-17-83, root request at 2179991110. Repro steps: they curl our API from onprem egress box: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` and sometimes see 220ms RTT (apac) other times 480ms (eu).
sre_oncall: can you dump the egress NAT translation at the time? conntrack or iptables state?
amy.k: customer provided partial conntrack snippets, pasted below. Note the source port mapping rotates every ~30s then flows start hitting eu-proxy according to logs.

amy.k: ```
# conntrack -L | grep 198.51.100.12
udp      17 src=198.51.100.12 dst=203.0.113.5 sport=52344 dport=443 packets=12 bytes=1440 [UNREPLIED] src=203.0.113.5 dst=198.51.100.12 sport=443 dport=52344 packets=10 bytes=1280 MARK=0
tcp      6 src=198.51.100.12 dst=203.0.113.5 sport=52345 dport=443 src=203.0.113.5 dst=198.51.100.12 sport=443 dport=52345 ESTABLISHED
```

vikram: interesting. If source port is changing, the egress proxy selection might be based on 5-tuple hashing that includes source port. If the onprem NAT uses port randomization/MASQUERADE, backend load balancers can pick a different region based on resulting tuple.
marco: also check if their NAT pool is small and sessions are being rotated (conntrack overflow) — can cause new outbound sockets to get different source ports and thus different egress path.
support_eng: did they mention any HA appliances like F5 or SD-WAN that could be re-sourcing flows across different ISP peers?
amy.k: yes: they have an SD-WAN cluster that performs active-active across two carriers. After the maintenance, flows started switching carriers more often.
sre_oncall: that explains the bounce. Two different carrier IPs are mapped -> upstream peering chooses different region-local proxies. Need to confirm mapping from their egress IP to our geo-routing table.
opsbot: [alert] route-flap-detect: FinServX egress IP 198.51.100.12 moved between carrier-1 and carrier-2 14 times in last 10m :eyes:
vikram: quick repro I'd ask the customer to run a steady curl loop that logs the resolved proxy FQDN and our http header with region: `for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | grep -i "x-redwood-region"; sleep 1; done` and capture src ip+port on the NAT box with `ss -tn sport = :443` snapshots.
marco: workaround options: 1) enable source IP preservation on their NAT (SNAT with static port mapping) so the 5-tuple is stable; 2) expand SNAT pool to avoid rapid port churn; 3) use source-based routing: route their VPC prefix to apac egress carrier; 4) on our side, add a sticky-hash that prefers region-siblings based on ASN / source IP prefix mapping (but that requires ops change).
support_eng: customer also sees occasional 403 auth errors when hitting eu proxy (fine on apac). Might be token audience or rate limit per-region. If requests land in different regions, auth counters could split and hit quota logic unexpectedly.
vikram: long-term we should tolerate moving source ports: our smart-routing currently uses a 5-tuple hash to pick proxy, which makes selection sensitive to NAT. We should consider fallbacks: 1) prefer routing by source IP prefix (3-tuple) first, 2) use short-lived session affinity keyed by backend cookie for HTTP keep-alive, or 3) accept multi-region by rekeying quotas per-account rather than per-proxy.
amy.k: customer asked for a quick mitigation they can do immediately. They applied a temp rule to preserve source ports on NAT (static-port on their NAT64) and expanded conntrack. After ~5m latency stabilized to apac.
sre_oncall: please attach timelines and conntrack dumps + curl loop output to the ticket and mark as escalated -> eng-runtime for routing policy review.
amy.k: attaching logs to ticket #FSX-4021. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
opsbot: deploy-bot: scheduled rollback of experimental rdf-routing-change at 2179993000 UTC (if not complete).
vikram: noted — we'll triage in eng-runtime tomorrow. For followups, please include: a) NAT config (masquerade vs snat, pool size), b) SD-WAN failover timers, c) samples of HTTP `X-Forwarded-For` and our `x-redwood-region` headers.
amy.k: will collect and post.
support_eng: marking thread resolved for customer temporary fix. Will keep open for engineering follow-up. :white_check_mark:
